articles.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
articles.summary: A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown. The same attack could be extended to reach the credentials Muse stores for the user's connected accounts. The work was a laboratory demonstration, not an attack on real users, and it stayed inside the individual user's

articles.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
articles.summary: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0,

articles.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
articles.summary: Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week. The flaw allows an attacker with no account to write files outside the server's storage folder, and it affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier in the default setup,

articles.title: Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
articles.summary: Signal has announced that it will restrict screenshots by default to stop artificial intelligence (AI) agents from reading private chats on Android and iOS devices, but conceded that the protection is "incomplete." The feature applies to agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where the encrypted messaging platform can detect an AI assistant attempting to read the Signal

articles.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added four flaws impacting Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and Broadcom VMware vCenter to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing evidence of active exploitation. articles.title: WhatsApp Patches 3 Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected of Use in Scams
articles.summary: Meta-owned WhatsApp has addressed security vulnerabilities, including one impacting its Android app that it suspects may have been exploited in connection with scam messages. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-23871 (CVSS score: 3.5), has been described as a case of incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs in WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4.

articles.title: Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays to Hide Credential Theft and Device Control
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously unknown Android malware framework called Bazuka that offers large language model (LLM) integration for victim management and control at scale. Dutch mobile security company ThreatFabric said it discovered the threat in late October 2026 during an investigation into an NFC-relay banking Trojan. "Bazuka is a full malware framework,

articles.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
articles.summary: A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean. On a shared server, that memory can include other customers' virtual machines. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled. Fixed kernels shipped

articles.summary: The BADBOX malware found in a broad range of generic Android TV boxes has returned to large-scale ad-fraud operations following last year's disruptions. [...]

articles.summary: FBI systems have reportedly been breached for the second time in two months, this time targeting the agency's National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used to share information between local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. [...]

articles.summary: Bell Canada has confirmed that an "agentic" threat actor breached its systems on November 17, 2026, and stole enterprise customer data, including information from a system used to order and provision telecommunications circuits. [...]

articles.title: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
articles.summary: Tracking company passwords in spreadsheets can leave IT administrators unaware of weak, reused, or compromised credentials stored and shared outside approved systems. NordPass explains how centralized password management can improve credential visibility, identify security risks, and simplify secure password sharing. [...]

articles.summary: Starting this week, Microsoft has begun automatically upgrading eligible devices that aren't managed by an IT department to Windows 11 26H2. [...]

articles.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
articles.summary: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

articles.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
articles.summary: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources

articles.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
articles.summary: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

articles.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

articles.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
articles.summary: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

articles.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
articles.summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices

articles.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

articles.title: China's 'Armory Castle' Lays Siege to VMware vCenter Zero-Day
articles.summary: During the last wave of major VMware vCenter security updates, a China-nexus threat group likely already had its next zero-day up its sleeve.
